population: Finnish men: Helsinki Birth Cohort Study (43 long-lived healthy, 92 controls who died at mean 66.6y) plus Helsinki Businessmen Study (63 healthy men, mean age 83); n=198 combined
conclusion: Discovery study for this variant. Combined two-tailed Fisher exact test gives OR 3.58 (95% CI 0.96-13.4, p=0.074) for the T allele in earlier-dying controls versus long-lived men, i.e. an inverse association between T and longevity that does not reach significance. Authors report study power of 28.4% and note the variant may be a marker rather than causal. Men only; no women were studied.
